prompt:
[confused, breathless] Iris?.. Where are we?.. Whose blood is this?

[quiet, anxious] What happened at home?

[quietly] No.

[shaky, determined] We're going back.

[barely audible, horrified] Iris… did I do it?

[nervous] Don't. I'll pay and go.

[trembling, desperate] I don't know what I did. Help my sister.

[soft, tired] Come with us.

[tense, firm] We can't take him.

[defeated, quiet] Fine. Get in the back.

[cold, firm] No. He stays.

[forced calm] It's going to be okay.

[broken, whispering] I don't know what's wrong with me.

[cold, flat] Drive. North.

[hurt, quiet] You really don't remember?

[tired, resigned] …Then drive.

[screaming] No!

[panicked, tearful] If we go back, they'll lock you up and put me in a home. Drive, Noah!

[cold, quiet] You don't remember. Then that's how it has to be.

[crying, desperate] Noah… It's suffering. Do something!

[nervous, distracted] There was a map in here somewhere…

[quiet, suspicious] You always hated them.

[gentle, soft] What are you doing out here all alone?

[urgent whisper] Get in. Now.

[gentle, reassuring] I'm right here. He won't hurt you.

[angry, pleading] Nobody's coming for him. You can see that.

[news announcer, neutral] …Victor, forty-nine, was found dead in his home. Police are searching for his children — his son Noah, nineteen, and his daughter Iris, fifteen. The son may be dangerous. If you have seen…

[news announcer, neutral] …about six feet tall, wearing a dark, old-fashioned man's jacket…
[scared, quiet] Mom told me to wait. She's been gone… a long time.

[gruff, reluctant] Go, kid. I'll make the call in ten minutes.

[wary, uneasy] Hey, kid…
